races.title: State Assembly, District 34
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Randall Putz
cands.bio: Small business owner and Big Bear Lake elected official. Served on the Bear Valley Unified School District board from 2008, then on the Big Bear Lake City Council from 2014, including as Mayor. Has chaired the Mountain Area Regional Transit Authority and the Big Bear Fire Authority. Opened Chirp Nature Center in 2018.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Democratic Party of California, the California Teachers Association, California Young Democrats, Equality California, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund (per Ballotpedia's endorsement list).

In his own survey answers, he lists endorsements from Communication Workers of America, San Bernardino County Professional Firefighters Local 935, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Superintendent Tony Thurmond, Sen. Tom Umberg, Rep. Norma Torres, and several Assemblymembers (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Putz was born, where he grew up, or when he moved to California. We found no specific statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. His campaign materials speak generally about building housing "smarter," protecting the environment, and funding public schools, but give no specifics. No documented controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had.

qual.background: Elected to the Bear Valley school board in 2008 and 2012, then to the Big Bear Lake City Council in 2014, 2018 and 2022, serving as Mayor Pro Tem and Mayor. Also a regional SCAG councilmember, a small business owner, and a marketing and technology consultant for corporate and government clients for over 25 years.
qual.why: Long local elected service and business ownership put him in the middle band. He has no prior state legislative service and no law, policy or state-budget career in the record.
qual.label: Long local elected service and business ownership put him in the middle band. He has no prior state legislative service and no law, policy or state-budget career in the record.

cands.name: Charles Frederick Hughes
cands.bio: Republican candidate for Assembly District 34. U.S. Navy veteran (1987-1990) and retired California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation lieutenant after 26 years. Small business owner with a restaurant. Antelope Valley Union High School District trustee and former board president.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California and Reform California, per Ballotpedia's endorsement list.
His campaign site lists endorsements from Heath Flora, Brian Jones, Shannon Grove, Suzette Valladares and Jay Obernolte, and from the Los Angeles County Republican Party endorsement lookup.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Hughes was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no record of how he voted on the school board or of bills he sponsored. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth limits, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or teacher pay. His campaign site names no donor-money pledges. The site's priorities page was cut off after the small business heading, so anything further down was not read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected Antelope Valley Union High School District trustee (board president from 2022, described as a two-term president). Spent 26 years with CDCR, rising to lieutenant. Served as a CCPOA chapter president and statewide supervisory vice president. Owns a small business.
qual.why: Local elected office, a long public-sector management career, union leadership and business ownership put him in the middle range. He has no prior legislative or budget-writing service.
qual.label: Local elected office, a long public-sector management career, union leadership and business ownership put him in the middle range. He has no prior legislative or budget-writing service.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Campaign site pledges property tax relief, including a $150,000 tax-free exemption on home values for veterans, and a middle-class tax cut.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Campaign site says he will expand school choice so parents, not government officials, decide where their children are educated.

back-police-order.evidence: Campaign site pledges to end early-release policies, stand against efforts to defund the police, protect the Peace Officer's Bill of Rights, and reinstate the death penalty. His Ballotpedia survey lists supporting law enforcement and increasing police presence as a key message.
